## Summary

Measure with the clock cycle counter (MOVEC CCC), align writes, prefer long and quad register updates, and do not unroll loops.

## Details

- Use the Clock Cycle Counter to see how many cycles your code took.

```text
   movec ccc,a6		; current counter
   <your code>
   movec ccc,d7
   sub.l a6,d7		; cycles used
```

- Mis-aligned memory reads (cache hit) cost no extra.
- Align writes for fastest result, so quad write to quad bound address.
- Conditional instruction, a faster way to execute a single following instruction after bcc.s.

```asm
   bcc.s skip
   <one_instruction>
skip
```

- Touch can preload the data cache.
- Prefer long & quad to update registers.

```text
   Internal the 68080 registers seem to be updated as long or quad.
   So updating a word or byte needs to read the source and destination (d2 & d3) to update the
   destination (d3)
	move.l   d2,d3 (read d2 , write that to d3)
	move.w d2,d3 (read top from d3 & bottom from d2, write that to d3)
   Both are executed in 1 cycle.
```

- Do not unroll loops. Stay in cache.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- Unrolling loops, a common 68000–68060 optimization, is discouraged on the 68080: stay in the cache.

## Do / Don't

- DO measure with `movec ccc,Rn` before and after your code.
- DO align writes: quad writes to quad-aligned addresses.
- DON'T unroll loops.
